title: Thirsty Sonnet
text:
My

you

. My thirst. My eve. My

I-love-you

.

The dagger and the wound that holds it.

The answer I wait for when I call.

My apple of heaven and of earth.


My

forever-and-ever

. My thin water,

moaning and blue. My love and sign.

Endless skin. The estranged rose.

The hollow-eyed garden that dreams me.


Stellar insomnia. What remains to me.

The apple again. The thirst. The silk.

My heart without use of reason:


you are missing from me so much in this distance,

in the afternoon, at night, by day,

as my heart itself would be missing from me.
editorial_note: This broken-line variant preserves the earlier English rendering while reflecting the source's fractured typography.

title: Sonnet with One Exception
text:
Everything is well: the green in the meadow,

the air with its diamond whistle,

and in the air the drawing branch,

and upward through the light the palm tree.


Everything is well: the forehead that waits for me,

the blue with its walking sky,

the damp red in the loving mouth,

and the homeland's wind in the flag.


Well that the infant should be among dreams,

that January should be blue and that I should sing.

Well the rose on its clear palfrey.


It is well that one should live and die.

The Sun, the Moon, the whole creation,

except my heart, everything is well.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's orderly inventory of goodness until the final exception of the heart.

title: I Heard Someone Climb the Stairs...
text:
I heard someone climb the stairs.

It was -high- three in the morning.

The dew and the bell were silent

... Only the faint creak of wood.


They were not my sons. It was not my daughter.

Nor the sound of time in my gray head.

(The window was delirious with stars.)

Nor the step my blood awaits...


A clock sounded in the deserted house.

Someone spoke my name and surname.

Named, I felt myself for the first time.


What passes in that voice

of familiar accent is not angel or friend...

... I felt someone climb the stairs...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the nocturnal suspense and the uncanny force of being named.

title: It Is Melancholy
text:
You will be called silence from now on.

And the place you occupied in the air

will be called melancholy.


I will write a name in the red wine:

your name that was beside my soul,

smiling among violets.


Now I look for a long time, absorbed,

at this hand that moved across your face,

that dreamed beside you.


This distant hand, from another world,

that knew one rose and another rose,

and the warm, the slow mother-of-pearl.


One day I will go looking for myself, I will go seeking

my thirsty ghost among the pines

and the word love.


You will be called silence from now on.

I write it with the hand that on that day

went with you among the pines.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the renaming of absence as silence and melancholy, and the hand as witness.

title: At Twenty...
text:
I come to kiss you for the detail...

I come to

        kiss you for the detail

of the Roquefort in the sandwich.

It had not

        occurred to you to mix it

with the ham and whole-wheat bread.

It does not

        matter that you interrupted

that uncertain writing. In

        truth

it was going nowhere. And above all

(the night was falling with

        its broken lineage

over us and over our children)

it was a

        pale imitation of some memorable

strawberries. Instead, this Roquefort

        still melted is alive.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Milán's intimate, comic turn from failed writing to the living detail of a sandwich.
